heading: Based on Spring, owned by Tachyon
body: OnStart marks the initialization method, and OnStop marks the cleanup method. An OnEvent method receives one payload (the value that comes with the event). Publishing works as in Spring. A class declares an applicationEventPublisher field with no initial value. Then it calls publishEvent(model) or publishEvent(model, retain). The event is the model: the name of its type is the event name, so a model named OrderPlaced in one language reaches a listener of the model OrderPlaced in any other language. The EventPublisher annotation is removed, and any use of it fails with TY1308. The reason: a method's return value is its answer to its caller, not an event. In Tac, Tachyon injects the field by its name, with or without Needs. In Yon, the field is a provider token that the container (the Tachyon part that creates providers) constructs. Needs binds it in exactly the same way as dataSource. A listener hears the model type of its one parameter. JavaScript reads that type from the JSDoc @param line. Before a listener runs, Tachyon checks the payload against its model with the same rules as a request body, and a payload that does not fit is not delivered. A listener can take replay, condition and id, but no event names (ADR 0055). ty migrate fix --write converts a listener whose event name matches a model. The Order(n) and InBackground modifiers go on the method. Each of these markers is compiler syntax on its own line. It is not a Spring package that runs at run time. The markers add no class-name or folder suffix beyond the existing role rules. A model marked Topic works like a Spring Cloud Bus remote event: its events also reach the listeners in other Yon languages and in open pages (see Topics).
